newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris, RJR Nabisco both post strong results.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris, RJR Nabisco both post strong results.

text.p: Two big food and tobacco companies reported strong second-quarter results Tuesday, with Philip Morris Cos. Inc. posting a 13 percent gain in profits and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. pulling out of the red after a restructuring.

The results were about in line with expectations on Wall Street, but Philip Morris stock rose $1.75 to $42.25 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues, and RJR Nabisco rose 75 cents to $30.56, also on the NYSE.
Philip Morris said net income for the quarter ended June 30 rose to $1.84 billion, or 76 cents a share, from $1.62 billion, or 66 cents a share.
The company, which makes Marlboro cigarettes, Miller beer and Kraft foods as well as other brands, said revenues climbed 5 percent to $18.4 billion from $17.5 billion.

It said tobacco revenues grew 11 percent to $10.2 billion from $9.2 billion while food sales declined 1.2 percent to $6.9 billion from $7 billion, mainly due to the adverse impact of currency fluctuations.
Philip Morris said earnings from tobacco jumed 13 percent to $2.3 billion from $2 billion while earnings from food rose 8 percent to $1.1 billion from $1.0 billion.
The New York-based company said shipments of Marlboro cigarettes rose almost 10 percent to 42.6 billion units, giving the brand a 34.6 percent share of industry sales, a gain of 3.2 points.
Its other premium brands, including Merit, Benson & Hedges, Parliament and Virginia Slims, accounted for 7.8 percent of industry shipments, down 0.3 points.

RJR Nabisco, whose business is about evenly split between tobacco and food products, mainly snacks, said it posted net income of $243 million, or 71 cents a share, compared with a year-earlier loss of $27 million, or 10 cents a share.
The 1996 results included a $428 million charge for restructuring the company's sales force.
The company -- which abandoned its controversial "Joe Camel" advertising character this month -- said total revenues edged up 2 percent to $4.29 billion from $4.20 billion.
Tobacco sales, fuelled by the Camel brand, rose 3 percent to $2.1 billion from $2 billion, with domestic sales rising to $1.22 billion from $1.17 billion.
Food sales grew to $2.19 billion from $2.18 billion, driven by strong growth in sales of its Oreo and other cookie brands. Life Savers candy and Planters snacks also performed well, the company said.
